title: Router registration: core vs product routes
answers: How do I register a new endpoint with the router?
Where do product routes get registered?
Why does RouterRegistry.add raise for products?
body:
- `posthog/api/routing.py:DefaultRouterPlusPlus` (drf-extensions ExtendedDefaultRouter, trailing slash optional `/?`).
- `posthog/api/rest_router.py`: creates `router`, then `projects_router = routers.add("projects", router.register(r"projects", project.RootProjectViewSet, "projects"))`; core viewsets: `projects_router.register(r"file_system", ViewSet, "project_file_system", ["team_id"])` (last arg = parent lookup kwargs).
- Products: expose `register_routes(routers)` in `products/<name>/backend/routes.py`; loop near end of rest_router.py finds them via INSTALLED_APPS, so no edit to rest_router.py is needed.
- `routing.py:RouterRegistry` exposes `routers.projects/organizations/root`; `add()` raises if called from `products.*` (parents are core-owned).
- `posthog/api/__init__.py` is a lazy shim; real aggregation is in rest_router.py.
- New team-nested endpoints: `routers.projects` with `project_<name>` basename; `/api/environments/` is a legacy alias (EnvironmentsRewriteMiddleware, per .agents/skills/improving-drf-endpoints/SKILL.md).
applies: Registering DRF viewsets; not for non-DRF Django URLs.
